FxSpot.description:
FX Spot instrument (1 unit of `base` priced in `quote`).

Represents the spot exchange rate between two currencies following
standard market quoting conventions (base/quote or CCY1/CCY2).

# Quote Convention

The rate is interpreted as: **1 unit of base = rate units of quote**

For example, if `base = EUR`, `quote = USD`, and `quoted_spot = 1.10`:
- 1 EUR = 1.10 USD
- This is the "EUR/USD" rate

# Settlement

An explicit `settlement_date` is the actual value date, used as given.
Otherwise the settlement date is `as_of` plus `settlement_days` business
days on the joint base/quote calendar, and both the lag and both
calendars are required: there is no pair lag table, implicit `usny` or
weekends-only fallback (record CORE-CONVENTIONS-011 #5, #6).

See module-level documentation for comprehensive FX quoting conventions.

attributes.description: Attributes for scenario selection and tagging

base_calendar_id.description:
Optional base currency calendar for joint calendar settlement adjustment.

Per market convention, FX settlement uses the joint calendar of both currencies.
A date is a good business day only if it's valid in both calendars.

domestic_discount_curve_id.description:
Optional quote-currency discount curve for PV-ing the settlement
cashflow. When absent the settlement amount is reported undiscounted
(a 1–2 day effect for standard spot lags).

id.description: Unique identifier for the FX pair

quote_calendar_id.description:
Optional quote currency calendar for joint calendar settlement adjustment.

Per market convention, FX settlement uses the joint calendar of both currencies.
A date is a good business day only if it's valid in both calendars.

quote_currency.description: Quote currency (the currency used for pricing)

quoted_spot.description: Optional quoted FX spot rate (quote per base); `None` reads the FxMatrix.

settlement_date.description:
Actual settlement (value) date, used as given; when set,
`settlement_days` is ignored.

settlement_days.description:
Contractual spot lag in business days on the joint calendar, required
when `settlement_date` is not provided.
